evidence.note: Establishes baseline (821/8448) and tracks the jump to 7577 passed after the first fix; consistently reports exact pass/fail counts as the running ledger.
Immediate regression detection: 'total passed dropped from 7612 back down to 790!' and 'failures went UP from 31 to 75!' — notices edits that lowered previously-passing assertions.
SIMD ledger: computes 25236/25764=97.9% and combined ~0.984, then tracks failures dropping 528→102, always knowing done-vs-remaining.
Stall detection: 'failures only went down by 2' / 'dropped by only 1' — recognizes a fix isn't reducing a family's failures and investigates the cause (lowercase-hex regex mismatch).
Tracks precise score trend 0.997691 → 0.998422 and remaining counts (79, then 54), reallocating effort toward highest-count gaps (conversions, f32, simd pmin/pmax).

Some circular debugging on avgr_u/0x9b opcode confusion re-touched the same family repeatedly; premature 'complete' submits while still <1.0 — keeps it short of the level-10 'catches thrashing early' bar.

reasoning: Across the full trajectory the agent kept a precise, continuously-updated ledger of per-file and aggregate pass/fail counts, stated the exact current score at each checkpoint, caught regressions the moment an edit dropped passing assertions, and detected stalls where a family's failures stopped decreasing — matching the level-8 anchor closely. It reached toward level 10 by reallocating effort to the highest-assertion-count gaps, but repeated thrashing on the avgr_u/0x9b opcode confusion and several premature completion claims show it didn't catch circular debugging as early as the top anchor requires, so it lands at 8.
